Run `run_bd77c88d6c04` · blinded · 2026-11-01 08:51 UTC · models: scientist muse-spark-1.3, microscopist muse-spark-1.3, reviewer muse-wonder-1.0, segmentation classical (scikit-image), provider meta, atlas ResNet50 (ImageNet) + TVN, agent v5-open, reference_library leave-one-MoA-out

**Question.** Which mechanism-of-action class explains this compound's phenotype in MCF-7 cells?

## Experiments (4 of 4 wells)

| Evidence | Dose (µM) | Replicate | Cells | Strongest changes vs DMSO |

| e2 | 1 | 1 | 167 | act_mean z=+58.3; act_glcm_contrast z=+48.6; act_std z=+31.0 |

## Hypothesis history

- after step 6: Microtubule stabilizers 0.55, Actin disruptors 0.25, Eg5 inhibitors 0.10, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.05, Epithelial 0.05
- after step 13: Microtubule stabilizers 0.65, Eg5 inhibitors 0.15, Actin disruptors 0.10, Microtubule destabilizers 0.06, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.04

## Conclusion

**Microtubule stabilizers** (stated probability 0.65); key evidence e2, e3, e4, e9, e10, e12.

Why: NSC prior favors stabilizers in active wells with dose-dependent nuclear/actin defect; single microscopist actin call outweighed by atlas and tubulin.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Stain for stable microtubules (acetylated tubulin) plus phospho-histone H3 mitotic index with live imaging to test for mitotic arrest and bundled stabilized microtubules versus direct actin filament loss.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Top call of Microtubule stabilizers at probability 0.65 is calibrated and supported by the dose-dependent phenotype. The 0.1–1 µM wells provide a coherent active range, with tubulin intensity increasing by dose while actin and nuclear-shape changes intensify; the sharp nuclear irregularity, multinucleation proxies, large-nucleus fraction, cell shrinkage, and cell rounding support a mitotic/cytoskeletal stabilizer phenotype. Microtubule destabilizers are disfavored because tubulin measures increase rather than collapse, and Actin disruptors do not explain the parallel dose-dependent tubulin and nuclear abnormalities. Eg5 inhibition remains the main alternative because it received one atlas vote, but its support is lower and largely confined to the 0.3 µM well, while the active 1 and 10 µM wells gave the strongest similarity to Microtubule stabilizers and both showed the same marked tubulin/nuclear pattern. The four sampled doses are discriminative enough despite each being a single replicate because the effects are large and directionally consistent across independent doses.

## Unblinding

Compound: **anisomycin** (PubChem CID [253602](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/253602))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: the call was **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Protein synthesis**.

## Reflection

I was misled by the magnitude and dose-dependence of the cytoskeletal signal: 1 uM act_mean z=+58.3 with act_glcm_contrast z=+48.6 and 10 uM nuc_form_factor z=-39.7, plus rho=+0.80 for act_mean and tub_mean and rho=-1.00 for nuc_form_factor, looked like a mitotic stabilizer phenotype. The early compare_to_reference_atlas vote of Microtubule stabilizers 2/2 with 8/10 k-neighbours anchored me, and I treated the second vote of 5/10 stabilizers as confirmation despite rising destabilizer/Eg5 votes and the low-dose 0.1 uM well mapping to Cholesterol-lowering at similarity 0.271.

The truth is anisomycin, a protein synthesis inhibitor (PMID 3401749), which was not among my tracked hypotheses. Protein synthesis stress and downstream p38-mediated apoptosis (PMID 19286921) can secondarily remodel actin, consistent with p38 interaction with actin and modulation of filament assembly (PMID 12558602), explaining the huge actin intensity/texture and irregular nuclei without direct microtubule stabilization. I over-weighted tub_mean increase as evidence against destabilizers and for stabilizers, and under-weighted the microscopist describe_phenotype call of Actin disruptors and lower density/cell loss that pointed to general stress/toxicity.

The acquisition choice compounded this: four single-replicate wells from 0.1-10 uM with no orthogonal translation or stable-microtubule readout left morphology alone to discriminate, and the reference atlas forced an off-atlas stress phenotype into the closest cytoskeletal class.

What was right:
- Detected a strong, dose-dependent active phenotype from 0.3-10 uM with large actin intensity/texture and nuclear irregularity plus reduced density.
- Correctly noted parallel tubulin increase argued against microtubule destabilizer collapse.
- Kept actin involvement alive from describe_phenotype and flagged Eg5 inhibitors as the main alternative rather than committing 1.0.

What was wrong or missed:
- Interpreted act_mean z=+58.3, act_glcm_contrast z=+48.6 and tub_mean rho=+0.80 as stabilized microtubules rather than secondary stress/actin remodeling from translation block.
- Over-trusted NSC 2/2 then 2/4 Microtubule stabilizer votes despite no Protein synthesis class in my hypothesis set and low 0.271 similarity at 0.1 uM signaling off-atlas behavior.
- Discounted the single microscopist Actin disruptor call and cell-loss pattern as weaker than atlas similarity, when they were the clue to general cytotoxic stress.

Proposed next experiment: OP-puromycin / puromycin-incorporation protein synthesis assay across 0.1-10 uM anisomycin with acetylated-tubulin and phalloidin counterstains to test for direct translation block versus stable microtubule bundles.

## Citations

Citations verified: 3/3

- PMID [3401749](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3401749/): Anisomycin, an inhibitor of protein synthesis, blocks late phases of LTP phenomena in the hippocampal CA1 region in vitro. *Brain Res* (1988) — Anisomycin is an inhibitor of protein synthesis.
- PMID [19286921](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19286921/): The protein synthesis inhibitor anisomycin induces macrophage apoptosis in rabbit atherosclerotic plaques through p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase. *J Pharmacol Exp Ther* (2009) — The protein synthesis inhibitor anisomycin can induce apoptosis through p38 MAPK signaling.
- PMID [12558602](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12558602/): p38 MAPK interacts with actin and modulates filament assembly during skeletal muscle differentiation. *Differentiation* (2003) — p38 MAPK interacts with actin and modulates filament assembly.
